q: Under AU-C 240, which of the following must the auditor presume is a fraud risk unless the presumption is rebutted?
choices: Improper revenue recognition
Misappropriation of petty cash
Understatement of accrued liabilities
Misstatement of related party disclosures
exp: AU-C 240 requires the auditor to presume there are risks of material misstatement due to fraud in revenue recognition and to evaluate which types of revenue or assertions give rise to them; the presumption can be rebutted with documentation. Petty cash misappropriation is rarely material and is not a presumed risk.

q: The risk of management override of controls is treated under AU-C 240 as:
choices: A risk that may be rebutted if management integrity is high
A significant risk present in all entities that cannot be rebutted
A risk only for entities with weak internal control
A risk addressed solely by tests of controls
exp: Because management override can occur in any entity, AU-C 240 treats it as a significant risk in all audits and requires specified procedures (journal entries, estimates, unusual transactions) regardless of other assessments. Unlike the revenue presumption, it cannot be rebutted.

q: Which of the following procedures is required in every audit to address the risk of management override of controls?
choices: Confirmation of all bank balances with zero-balance accounts
Observation of inventory counts at every location
Retrospective review of management judgments and assumptions in significant accounting estimates reflected in the prior year
Surprise cash counts at year-end
exp: AU-C 240 requires testing journal entries, reviewing accounting estimates for bias including a retrospective review of prior-year estimates, and evaluating the business rationale of significant unusual transactions. The other procedures may be useful responses but are not universally required.

q: A divisional controller is paid a bonus based on division earnings and faces aggressive targets set by headquarters. This condition is best classified among the fraud risk factors as:
choices: An opportunity
A rationalization
An attitude
An incentive or pressure
exp: Compensation tied to aggressive targets creates an incentive or pressure to commit fraudulent financial reporting. Opportunity relates to circumstances such as weak controls, and attitude/rationalization relates to a mindset that justifies the act.

q: During the engagement team discussion required by AU-C 240, the team should emphasize:
choices: How and where the entity's financial statements might be susceptible to material misstatement due to fraud, setting aside beliefs about management's honesty
The prior-year conclusion that management has high integrity, which allows reduced skepticism
Which team members will be assigned to test cash
The client's planned dividend policy
exp: The brainstorming discussion focuses on how fraud could occur and be concealed, and requires members to set aside any belief that management is honest. Relying on prior beliefs about integrity undermines professional skepticism.

q: An auditor discovers that a warehouse clerk stole inventory worth an immaterial amount. Under AU-C 240, the auditor should:
choices: Ignore the matter because it is immaterial
Bring the matter to the attention of an appropriate level of management on a timely basis
Withdraw from the engagement immediately
Report the matter directly to law enforcement
exp: When the auditor has evidence that fraud may exist, AU-C 240 requires communicating it to an appropriate level of management, even if inconsequential. Fraud involving senior management or causing material misstatement goes to those charged with governance; external reporting is generally not the auditor's duty absent legal requirements.

q: Which of the following best describes the inherent limitation the auditor faces with respect to fraud detection?
choices: The auditor is not required to consider fraud in a financial statement audit
Fraud resulting from error is harder to detect than fraud resulting from intentional acts
The risk of not detecting a material misstatement due to fraud is higher than for error because fraud may involve collusion, forgery, and concealment
Auditors are responsible for detecting all frauds regardless of materiality
exp: AU-C 240 explains that fraud is harder to detect than error because it can involve sophisticated concealment, collusion, and management override. Error is by definition unintentional, and the auditor's responsibility is reasonable assurance regarding material misstatement.

q: An auditor identifies a misstatement due to fraud that is not material and involves a mid-level purchasing manager. Which is the most appropriate response?
choices: Conclude that the matter has no implications beyond the specific item
Discontinue the audit because management representations are now unreliable
Communicate only in the auditor's report
Reevaluate the assessment of fraud risk and consider the implications for other aspects of the audit, including the reliability of representations
exp: AU-C 240 requires the auditor to consider whether an identified misstatement may indicate fraud and its implications, since fraud is unlikely to be an isolated occurrence; the auditor reevaluates risks and the reliability of representations. Immaterial fraud does not automatically require withdrawal.

q: Which of the following responses to an assessed fraud risk at the overall financial statement level best incorporates unpredictability?
choices: Performing procedures at locations or on accounts not normally tested, without advance notice to the entity
Performing the same procedures as the prior year so results are comparable
Using larger samples drawn from the same population tested last year
Reducing reliance on substantive procedures
exp: AU-C 240 requires incorporating an element of unpredictability, such as testing locations or balances not normally examined or changing timing. Repeating prior-year procedures is predictable, and merely increasing the sample size in the same area adds little unpredictability.

q: When selecting journal entries to test for management override, the auditor should give particular attention to entries that:
choices: Are system-generated and recurring each month
Are made at the end of the reporting period, posted by individuals who do not usually make entries, or contain round numbers
Relate to cash receipts that have been confirmed
Were reviewed by the external auditor in the prior year
exp: AU-C 240 directs the auditor to focus on entries with fraud-risk characteristics, such as period-end entries, unusual preparers, unrelated or seldom-used accounts, and round numbers. Routine system-generated entries are generally lower risk, though not ignored.

q: An auditor rebuts the presumption that revenue recognition is a fraud risk for a client with a single, simple revenue stream of lease rentals. What is required?
choices: The auditor must obtain written approval from those charged with governance
No documentation is required if the risk is rebutted
The auditor must document the reasons supporting the conclusion that the presumption does not apply
The auditor must still treat revenue as a significant risk
exp: AU-C 240 permits rebutting the revenue presumption in limited circumstances but requires documentation of the reasons. Rebuttal means the auditor does not treat it as a fraud risk; approval by governance is not required.

q: Which of the following is an example of misappropriation of assets rather than fraudulent financial reporting?
choices: Recording fictitious sales near year-end to meet analyst expectations
Intentionally omitting disclosure of a guarantee
Deliberately understating the allowance for credit losses
Lapping of customer payments to conceal theft of cash receipts
exp: Lapping conceals theft of cash, so it is misappropriation of assets. Fictitious sales, omitted disclosures, and manipulated estimates are intentional misstatements of the financial statements, which is fraudulent financial reporting.

q: An auditor identifies a significant unusual transaction outside the normal course of business: a sale of land to an entity whose ownership is unclear, recorded on the last day of the year at a large gain. The auditor should primarily:
choices: Evaluate whether the business rationale suggests the transaction may have been entered into to engage in fraudulent financial reporting or conceal misappropriation
Accept the transaction because it was approved by the CFO
Limit work to vouching the cash receipt
Treat the transaction as a subsequent event
exp: AU-C 240 requires evaluating whether the business rationale (or lack of it) of significant unusual transactions suggests fraud. CFO approval alone does not address override risk, and the transaction occurred within the period.

q: Which of the following inquiries is required by AU-C 240 during risk assessment?
choices: Inquiry of the entity's external legal counsel about fraud
Inquiry of management and others within the entity, including internal audit if applicable and those charged with governance, about knowledge of fraud or suspected fraud
Inquiry of all employees through a written survey
Inquiry of the predecessor auditor about client fees
exp: AU-C 240 requires inquiries of management, appropriate others, internal audit, and those charged with governance about fraud risks and known or suspected fraud. Legal counsel and surveys of all employees are not required by the standard.

q: An auditor concludes that the financial statements are materially misstated due to fraud involving the CEO and that the CEO dominates the board. Which is most appropriate?
choices: Issue an unmodified opinion with an emphasis-of-matter paragraph
Report the fraud to the SEC before discussing with anyone at the entity
Consider withdrawing from the engagement where permitted and obtain legal advice, in addition to required communications
Expand sample sizes and continue without communication
exp: AU-C 240 indicates that when fraud raises questions about the auditor's ability to continue, the auditor considers professional and legal responsibilities, including possible withdrawal and legal advice. An emphasis-of-matter paragraph cannot cure a material misstatement.

q: In which situation is the auditor most likely to have a duty to disclose fraud to parties outside the entity?
choices: When the fraud involves only immaterial misappropriation
When the client asks the auditor to keep the matter confidential
When the auditor believes the board has acted appropriately
In response to a subpoena or to a successor auditor's inquiries, with client permission where required
exp: AU-C 240 notes the auditor's ethical duty of confidentiality generally precludes external reporting, but disclosure may be appropriate under legal requirements such as a subpoena, to successor auditors (with consent), or as required by law or regulation. Immateriality does not create an outside reporting duty.

q: Which of the following is an opportunity risk factor for fraudulent financial reporting?
choices: Significant related-party transactions not in the ordinary course of business with unaudited related entities
Management's excessive interest in maintaining the stock price
Threats of bankruptcy
Management's history of violating securities laws
exp: Complex or unusual related-party transactions provide an opportunity to misstate. Interest in the stock price and bankruptcy threats are incentives/pressures, and a history of violations reflects attitude/rationalization.

q: An auditor is evaluating accounting estimates for possible management bias. Which observation is most indicative of bias?
choices: Each estimate is individually reasonable, and estimates are evenly distributed around point estimates
Each estimate is individually within a reasonable range, but all fall at the end of the range that increases earnings
The client uses a specialist for its pension valuation
Estimates changed due to new information that became available
exp: AU-C 240 and AU-C 540 note that individually reasonable estimates that consistently favor one direction may collectively indicate management bias. Changes due to new information or use of specialists are not themselves indicators of bias.

q: An auditor observes that physical inventory counts at the main warehouse are performed with the auditor present but that management requested no auditor attendance at a satellite location. Which response is most appropriate?
choices: Accept management's request because the satellite is smaller
Rely on the main warehouse count to cover all locations
Treat the request as a possible fraud risk factor and consider attending or performing unannounced counts at the satellite location
Disclaim an opinion immediately
exp: Management limiting auditor access to particular locations can signal fraud risk; the auditor responds with unpredictable procedures such as surprise counts at that location. A disclaimer is premature until the auditor determines whether evidence can be obtained.

q: Which of the following is required documentation under AU-C 240?
choices: A list of every employee interviewed during the audit
The fee arrangements with the client
A copy of the client's code of conduct
The significant decisions reached during the engagement team discussion, the identified and assessed fraud risks, and the auditor's responses
exp: AU-C 240 requires documenting the team discussion and significant decisions, identified and assessed risks of material misstatement due to fraud, responses, results of procedures, and communications. A list of every employee interviewed and fee arrangements are not required by AU-C 240.

q: Which statement best describes the auditor's responsibility for detecting fraud under AU-C 240?
choices: To obtain reasonable assurance that the financial statements as a whole are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error
To guarantee that no fraud has occurred
To detect all misappropriation of assets regardless of amount
To prevent fraud through recommendations on internal control
exp: The auditor's objective is reasonable assurance about material misstatement whether caused by fraud or error; prevention and detection are primarily the responsibility of management and those charged with governance. No audit can guarantee absence of fraud.

q: An auditor learns that an employee anonymous hotline complaint alleges that sales personnel are entering into side agreements granting customers unlimited return rights. Which procedure best responds?
choices: Increase the sample of cash disbursements tested
Confirm with customers the terms of sales, including the absence of side agreements and return rights
Recompute depreciation expense
Review the minutes of the compensation committee only
exp: Confirming contract terms directly with customers, including side agreements, is a recommended response in AU-C 240 to revenue fraud risks. Disbursements and depreciation are unrelated to the alleged revenue manipulation.

q: Under PCAOB AS 2401 for an issuer audit, if the auditor determines there is evidence that fraud may exist involving senior management, the auditor should communicate directly to:
choices: The SEC within one business day
Only the CFO
The audit committee
The PCAOB inspections staff
exp: AS 2401 requires fraud involving senior management, or fraud causing material misstatement, to be reported directly to the audit committee. Direct reporting to the SEC arises only under specific Section 10A procedures when the board fails to act appropriately.

q: An auditor's analytical procedures performed near the end of the audit reveal that revenue recognized in the last week of the year is unusually high relative to prior weeks. Under AU-C 240, the auditor should:
choices: Conclude no further action is needed because the overall review is not required to detect fraud
Reduce materiality for revenue
Defer consideration to the next audit
Evaluate whether the result indicates a previously unrecognized risk of material misstatement due to fraud
exp: AU-C 240 requires the auditor to evaluate whether analytical procedures performed near the end of the audit indicate a previously unrecognized risk of material misstatement due to fraud. Deferring or ignoring the unusual trend would fail that requirement.

q: Which of the following is the most likely reason the auditor would test the reconciliation of the general ledger to the trial balance used to prepare the financial statements?
choices: To determine that entries and adjustments made in preparing the financial statements, including post-closing entries, are captured for testing
To satisfy the going-concern evaluation
To determine materiality
To evaluate the work of internal audit
exp: AU-C 240 requires testing entries made in preparing the financial statements, which may bypass the general ledger; reconciling the ledger to the statements helps identify top-side and post-closing adjustments. The reconciliation is unrelated to materiality or going concern.

q: An auditor finds that several shipping documents supporting year-end sales appear altered. The auditor is not trained to authenticate documents. Which is most appropriate?
choices: Accept the documents as genuine because auditors are not expected to authenticate documents
Investigate further, possibly including confirmation with third parties or use of a specialist to assess authenticity
Remove the sales from the population and continue sampling
Issue a disclaimer of opinion immediately
exp: Although auditors are not trained as document authentication experts, AU-C 240 and AU-C 500 require further investigation when conditions indicate a document may not be authentic, such as confirmation or using a specialist. Simply accepting suspicious documents violates professional skepticism.

q: Which of the following is most likely a fraud risk factor relating to attitudes/rationalizations?
choices: Inadequate segregation of duties in the cash function
Rapid growth relative to the industry
Management's practice of committing to analysts to achieve aggressive forecasts and a strained relationship with the current auditor
High dependence on debt financing with restrictive covenants
exp: AU-C 240 lists aggressive commitments to analysts and a strained relationship with the auditor as attitude/rationalization factors. Weak segregation is an opportunity, and rapid growth and debt covenants are pressures.

q: An auditor concludes, after performing procedures, that a material misstatement due to fraud exists but management refuses to correct it. What opinion is appropriate, assuming the effect is material but not pervasive?
choices: Unmodified with an other-matter paragraph
Disclaimer of opinion
Adverse opinion
Qualified opinion
exp: An uncorrected material misstatement that is material but not pervasive results in a qualified opinion under AU-C 705, regardless of whether it stems from fraud or error. An adverse opinion is used when the misstatement is pervasive, and a disclaimer relates to inability to obtain evidence.

q: Which is the most appropriate response to an assessed fraud risk related to inventory quantities at multiple locations?
choices: Observe counts at all locations on the same date or perform counts at selected locations on an unannounced basis
Rely on management's perpetual records without observation
Perform analytical procedures on gross margin only
Request a representation that inventory exists
exp: AU-C 240 suggests simultaneous or unannounced counts as responses to inventory fraud risk, preventing the transfer of goods between locations. Analytics and representations alone do not adequately address the risk of fictitious quantities.

q: An auditor assesses a fraud risk related to the allowance for credit losses at the assertion level. Which response is most appropriately tailored to that risk?
choices: Increase overall materiality to reduce testing
Obtain more reliable and relevant evidence, such as independently evaluating subsequent collections and testing the data and assumptions underlying the estimate
Rely primarily on inquiry of the credit manager
Perform the same procedures used for low-risk accounts at an interim date
exp: AU-C 240 requires responses to assertion-level fraud risks that change the nature, timing, or extent of procedures, such as obtaining more reliable evidence and testing assumptions. Inquiry alone is weak evidence, and interim-only procedures may be less effective for a period-end estimate.
